mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D engine replacement typically costs £600-£1,400 for a used unit, £1,400-£2,400 for reconditioned, and £2,400-£3,800 for a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Specialist fitting costs add £500-£800.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N13 1.8 DI-D diesel is considered the weak point of the ASX range. Early models (2010-2013) suffered from turbocharger failures, piston ring carbon buildup, and frequent DPF regeneration cycles. Mitsubishi issued two recalls for the 1.8 DI-D. However, with regular maintenance and the ECU recall applied, many units have proven durable.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N13 1.8 DI-D engine uses a timing chain, not a belt. Chains are designed to last the engine's lifetime, but rely on clean, correct-spec engine oil. Regular oil and filter changes are essential - sludge can clog the hydraulic tensioner and accelerate chain wear.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbo failure on an ASX 1.8 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include a loud whining or siren-like noise from the engine, sudden loss of power, black smoke from the exhaust, and a check engine light. The 4N13 is known for sudden turbo failure caused by the intake duct seal detaching and being sucked into the turbocharger.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a 2010-2016 Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: With 2010-2015 ASX 1.8 DI-D values ranging from £3,000-£8,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,400-£3,800 represents 30-60% of the vehicle's value. For sub-£4,000 examples, a used engine is usually the sensible choice. If your ASX is in excellent condition and low-mileage, a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty can be a viable option.

mainEntity.name: What was the Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D recall about?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mitsubishi issued a recall for 8,079 ASX vehicles with the 1.8 DI-D engine (2010-2013) to reprogram the engine ECU. This was to address excessive carbon buildup causing piston ring sticking and oil consumption. A separate recall affected 18,250 ASX vehicles (2014-2016) for tailgate supports, and 17,971 vehicles (2011-2015) for windscreen wiper linkage joints.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The first-generation Mitsubishi ASX (GA_W_) launched in the UK in 2010, with the 1.8 DI-D 4N13 diesel offered from launch as one of the core powertrains . The 4N13 was available in two states of tune - 116PS and 150PS - and remained in production through to 2016, when it was replaced by the PSA-sourced 9HD 1.6 diesel and the larger 4N14 2.2 diesel .

milestones.description: ASX launched in the UK with 4N13 1.8 DI-D diesel engine (116PS and 150PS variants)
2013 - Early 4N13 units affected by turbocharger failures and piston ring carbon buildup; two recalls issued
4N13 phased out in favour of 9HD 1.6 DI-D diesel and 4N14 2.2 DI-D
First-generation ASX production ends; no direct successor in UK market

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi ASX 1.8 DI-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4N13 1.8 DI-D diesel is the known Achilles' heel of the ASX range . While other ASX engines (petrol) have proven reliable, the early 4N13 diesel suffered from multiple well-documented issues including turbocharger failure, piston ring carbon buildup, and DPF regeneration problems . Mitsubishi issued two recalls affecting early 4N13 units . Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - The 4N13's Most Frequent and Costly Issue
problems.rootCause: The air intake duct seal can detach and be sucked into the turbocharger, causing catastrophic impeller damage . Owners report sudden turbo failure with loud whining noise, loss of power, and black smoke . One owner reported a £3,000+ repair bill for turbo failure at just 80,000km . The turbocharger also suffers from oil supply issues and carbon buildup on VNT mechanisms.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or recon turbocharger, oil feed line, intake duct, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before turbo debris has damaged the engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt 4N13 with upgraded turbo and piston rings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo debris has damaged pistons/cylinders

problems.recommendation: If your ASX 1.8 DI-D suffers turbo failure, first check if your vehicle is covered under the Mitsubishi ECU recall (2010-2013 models) . If out of warranty, have the engine inspected for debris damage - if the turbo has disintegrated, metal particles may have circulated through the engine and damaged pistons, rings, and bearings. For high-mileage examples with engine damage, a used engine often offers better value than a rebuild. However, if the car is in excellent condition and you plan to keep it, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components and 12-month warranty is the safest option.

problems.group: Piston Ring Carbon Buildup and Excessive Oil Consumption
problems.h4: Piston Ring Carbon Buildup and Excessive Oil Consumption
problems.rootCause: Carbon deposits can cause the piston rings to stick in their grooves, leading to bore glazing and excessive oil consumption . Mitsubishi issued a recall for 8,079 vehicles with the 1.8 DI-D (2010-2013) to reprogram the engine ECU to address this issue .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine ECU software update to modify combustion parameters
repairOptions.longevity: First-line fix; may be covered by recall

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Oil change with correct low-SAPS oil; DPF regeneration check; fuel additive treatment
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is mild; can extend engine life

problems.recommendation: Check if your ASX 1.8 DI-D VIN is covered by the ECU recall . If you're experiencing excessive oil consumption (1L or more per 1,000 miles), have the engine inspected for bore glazing. At this stage, full replacement is rarely needed; a professional decarbonisation service and ECU update often resolves the issue.

problems.group: DPF Regeneration Frequency and Oil Dilution
problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Frequency and Oil Dilution
problems.rootCause: Frequent DPF regeneration cycles (particularly in urban use) can cause diesel fuel to dilute the engine oil . This reduces oil viscosity and lubrication, accelerating wear on the turbocharger and timing chain.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: DPF regeneration, oil and filter change with correct low-SAPS oil
repairOptions.longevity: Regular maintenance; essential for urban-driven examples

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Software update to refine DPF regeneration strategy

problems.recommendation: If your ASX 1.8 DI-D is used primarily for short urban trips, schedule regular motorway runs to allow the DPF to regenerate properly. Use only the correct low-SAPS engine oil (C1/C2 specification) and change it at 6,000-8,000 mile intervals rather than the factory 12,500-mile schedule. Check your VIN against the ECU recall - this update reduces the frequency of regeneration cycles .
